title: Game Development Schedule for RPG Maker games

posts.author: Frankerlin
posts.body:
Hi there folks!
I am very curious about how you guys organise the development schedule of your RPG Maker games - or games in general.
How do you start?
Do you start with the story and concept? The music? Do you see a cool game sprite and imagine the character then the game they could star in? Or maybe you start with the locations/tilesets?
Are you structured and go from story/characters, then tilesets/sprites/battlers? Or do you tend to dip your toe in each part and change things as you go along, based on how you are feeling at the time?
And if you are the organised type, do you keep track of things via spreadsheet, trello and/or other platforms?
I look forward to hearing your approaches!

posts.author: Timeline_man
posts.body:
being an entirely solo dev who has a full-time job besides... Time management isn't an exact formula to me. I have 1-2 days a week set to get
something
done, doesn't matter how small. So the important thing to have there is a design document, so you can refresh yourself on what needs to get done if/when you forget something along the path of working on something else.
I am a rather impulsive type, though. If I feel like drawing, then I'll do sprites, CGs, tiles or whatever. If I feel like writing, I'll throw a scene together, and so on so forth.

posts.author: Artille
posts.body:
There is no secret formula as far as I know.
The best part to make progress on is that part that makes you want to continue!
It could be anything, lore, music, gameplay, mechanics, UI, easter eggs, logic, or even that friggin cool hidden NPC's background story... so long as you enjoy it "right now", then that's what you wanna do ^^
Everyone has their beloved pattern.
If you ask me (since you asked general opinion), I like to start with the lore.
I tried different approaches, but not knowing where to go (as a general idea) usually makes me wander and lose time on side-side-side quests that looks cool when in the making, but just plays horrible in the end ^^
So, new me works on the lore first, creating character I really like, imagining their background story and relations, and from there on filling with side characters that can enrich my main characters.
Then, when making the actual game, I have a much better vision of what I'm going for.
Though, this wouldn't apply to a game like pong (or with almost no story like a roguelite)

posts.author: mirrormagic
posts.body:
As a student who spends a majority of the day at school (or doing stuff for school), I try to get whatever I can done in the pockets of free time I have, like when I complete assignments early.
Currently I'm working on a game and I have the general idea for the characters down, but I'm just trying to polish the story in my Word doc.
Aside from that though I'm also just messing around in Aseprite trying to draw the maps and portraits for everyone, and so far it's been pretty fun! Once I have a very clear grasp on how I want the plot to do, that's when I'll probably focus on making everything in RPGMAKER, and once that's done, it'll just be ironing all the problems until something good comes out.

posts.author: gabbysogabby
posts.body:
1,Story concept for zone/chapter
2. the battle enemies sprites and their pixel overworld sprites
3.make the art map
4.flesh out the initial story
5.code it all in  (i try not to do anything too complex, so this barely takes an hour)
6. play test for a bit
7. release update
I sent a one month deadline for myself, and if I can't get it done by then, I just release it at the current state and fix it later

posts.author: Frankerlin
posts.body:
Some good responses here! A couple of you mentioned being a student and having a full-time job (I am in the latter category) so I can relate to trying to find those pockets of time among an already busy life!
Artille, your suggestion about choosing the parts that motivate you to continue is solid, too. You say that you like to work on the lore and characters first so you have more of an idea of what you're doing, which is what I am trying to do, interweaving it with other tasks like mapping, item creation etc when I feel like I wanna switch things up.

posts.author: vigamanufacture
posts.body:
My development schedule looks exactly like my job: no schedule, just chaos disguised as planning. To answer you though:
How do I start? Usually with the concept or vibe first, like management calling a meeting without an agenda. Story, art, music all get stapled on after.
Do I start with story/music/tilesets? Story and concept lead, but sometimes I see a sprite and think, ‘Fine, you’re first priority.’
Structured or dipping toes? I dip into everything at once, because like at work no one ever gives me the time to finish one task before piling on three more.
Organized with spreadsheets/Trello? Tried spreadsheets... it ended up looking like my performance review: half empty, outdated, and quietly mocking me. Now I just track progress in my head and hope HR doesn’t ask for updates.
